title: Bit Manipulation & Bitmask Tricks
relevance: High (XOR / popcount / subset masks show up constantly in OAs; bitmask DP is the CM stretch)
company_notes: XOR uniqueness (every element twice except one, or thrice / two singles) — FAANG phone-screen Single Number family. Subset/flag masks with n ≤ 15–20 on/off choices (lock dials, team splits, knapsack-like partition) → 2^n bitmasks, often unnamed. Bitwise score / maximize AND-OR: flip at most k bits or OR values to maximize AND / minimize XOR — Amazon / Google OA style. Hidden bit DP: assignment / elevator / TSP-on-n≤20 — interviewers call it DP; encoding is a bitmask over used people/nodes.

phases.goal: Establish when the candidate reaches for bit primitives, XOR uniqueness, 2^n masks, or bitmask DP instead of naive loops.

must_hit.point: Statement cues: "bitwise", small n, "differ in at most k bits", powers of two, or "minimum / maximum AND/OR/XOR".
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names those wording/constraint signals as the trigger to think in bits.

must_hit.point: "Every element appears twice except one" (or thrice / two singles) → XOR uniqueness / Single Number family.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps the pair-cancel story to XOR and may cite Single Number / Single Number III.

must_hit.point: n ≤ 15–20 items with on/off choices (lock dials, team splits, partition) → enumerate 2^n bitmasks, even if the statement never says "bitmask".
must_hit.evidence_hint: Points at Petr lock / Apple Division / Subsets-style mask search under n ≤ 15 or n ≤ 20.

must_hit.point: Assignment / elevator / TSP-on-n≤20 graphs: state is the set of used people/nodes; interviewers say DP, the encoding is a bitmask.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Elevator Rides / Matching / hidden bit DP as mask-encoded used-set DP.

probes: What in the statement makes you reach for XOR cancel, popcount, or a 2^n mask instead of nested loops?
When do you treat an interview "DP" problem as a bitmask over a used set?

hints.1: Look for bitwise wording, powers of two, Hamming-like "differ in bits", or tiny n with yes/no choices.
hints.2: Pair-cancel uniqueness → XOR; n ≤ 15–20 on/off → 2^n; used people/nodes ≤20 → mask DP.
hints.3: Say: Single Number XOR; Fedor-style Hamming via XOR+popcount; Petr/Apple/Subsets 2^n; Elevator/Matching bitmask DP.

phases.goal: Get the candidate to state bit-set ops, XOR/prefix-XOR identities, mask enumeration, and the bitmask DP template before coding.

must_hit.point: Treat integers as sets of bits: AND / OR / XOR + shifts give O(1) set ops; n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit; n & -n isolates it.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States clear-lowest vs isolate-lowest and O(1) set-style bit ops.

must_hit.point: XOR cancels pairs (x⊕x=0, x⊕0=x); subarray XOR via prefix identity a[l..r] = pref[r] ⊕ pref[l-1]; find the one (or two) unique element(s).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes the prefix-XOR identity and the pair-cancel uniqueness approach.

must_hit.point: When n ≤ 20, encode subsets as masks and enumerate 2^n (or 3^n submasks).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says mask = subset of {0..n-1}, loop 0..2^n-1, or submask iteration for 3^n.

must_hit.point: Bitmask DP template: dp[mask], transition by adding one element or merging a submask; Elevator / Matching style states.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes dp[mask] with add-one or submask merges and cites Elevator or Matching.

probes: State the clear-lowest and isolate-lowest bit tricks, and the prefix-XOR range identity.
When n ≤ 20, how do you encode subsets, and when do you move from plain 2^n search to dp[mask]?

hints.1: Separate bit primitives, XOR identities, and mask search/DP.
hints.2: Clear with n&(n-1); isolate with n&-n; range XOR from two prefixes; masks when n ≤ 20.
hints.3: Say: O(1) AND/OR/XOR/shifts; clear/isolate lowest; a[l..r]=pref[r]⊕pref[l-1]; 2^n / 3^n; dp[mask] Elevator/Matching.

phases.goal: Confirm the candidate can write popcount/power-of-two checks, bit primitives, mask/submask loops, and core DP/trie templates from memory.

must_hit.point: Popcount via Brian Kernighan n &= n-1; power-of-two test n & (n-1) == 0; Counting Bits recurrence dp[i] = dp[i>>1] + (i&1).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Writes n&=n-1 for popcount, the power-of-two check, and the right-shift DP recurrence.

must_hit.point: Bit primitives: test / set / clear / toggle bit i; isolate lowest set bit (x & -x); clear it (x & (x-1)); popcount / ctz / clz (or builtins).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists those primitives and may mention __builtin_popcount / ctz / clz.

must_hit.point: Power set: for mask in 0..2^n-1 take set bits; Gray code with i ^ (i >> 1); submasks via for (sub = mask; sub; sub = (sub-1)&mask).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches the mask loop, Gray formula, and the (sub-1)&mask submask idiom.

must_hit.point: Elevator-style state dp[mask] = (rides, last weight); Hamming friends via __builtin_popcount(x^y) <= k; Single Number III partitions by lowest set bit.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Elevator pair-state, Fedor popcount(x^y), or XOR-partition by lowest set bit for two singles.

probes: Write popcount with n &= n-1 and the power-of-two check from memory.
How do you enumerate all subsets or all submasks of a mask, and what does Elevator store in dp[mask]?

hints.1: Start from Kernighan clear-lowest and the power-of-two equality.
hints.2: Add isolate x&-x, mask 0..2^n-1, and the (sub-1)&mask loop.
hints.3: Say: n&=n-1 popcount; n&(n-1)==0; x&-x; Subsets/Gray/submask loops; Elevator (rides, last weight); popcount(x^y).

phases.goal: State the cost of bit ops, 2^n / 3^n enumeration, SOS, and the XOR-trie regime.

must_hit.point: AND / OR / XOR + shifts give O(1) set ops on integers-as-bitsets.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls bit set ops constant-time per operation.

must_hit.point: Enumerate all subsets when n ≤ 20 in 2^n; iterate submasks in O(3^n).
must_hit.evidence_hint: States 2^n for subsets and O(3^n) for submask enumeration / Grouping-style DP.

must_hit.point: SOS / subset-zeta pushes along each bit dimension in O(2^B · B); XOR binary trie on 30–31 bits for max XOR pair / max XOR subarray.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names O(2^B · B) SOS and a 30–31-bit XOR trie for max pref[r]⊕pref[l-1].

probes: What are the costs of plain bit ops versus full subset or submask enumeration?
When do you quote O(2^B · B) SOS or a 30–31-bit XOR trie instead of 2^n search?

hints.1: Separate O(1) primitives from exponential mask work.
hints.2: n ≤ 20 → 2^n; submasks → O(3^n); SOS and tries are the stretch costs.
hints.3: Say: O(1) AND/OR/XOR/shifts; 2^n subsets; O(3^n) submasks; SOS O(2^B · B); XOR trie on 30–31 bits.

phases.goal: Surface confuse-the-primitive, broken prefix XOR, and missed mask/Hamming signals that fail these problems.

must_hit.point: Confusing isolate-lowest (x & -x) with clear-lowest (x & (x-1)) breaks popcount loops and Single Number III-style partitions.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Separates isolate vs clear and ties each to the right template.

must_hit.point: Computing subarray XOR without the prefix identity a[l..r] = pref[r] ⊕ pref[l-1].
must_hit.evidence_hint: States the two-prefix XOR form used in Range Xor Queries / max-XOR-subarray setups.

must_hit.point: Missing that Hamming distance is popcount of XOR (friends iff __builtin_popcount(x^y) <= k), or that AND never increases so AND-of-all can be optimal.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Cites Fedor-style XOR+popcount and Mocha-style AND-never-increases.

must_hit.point: Treating n ≤ 15–20 on/off or used-set DP as generic search/DP without encoding the state as a bitmask.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says the interview DP is still a mask over chosen/used indices (Petr / Elevator / Matching).

probes: What goes wrong if you mix up x & -x with x & (x-1)?
How do you get range XOR from prefixes, and how do you recognize Hamming-via-XOR?

hints.1: Check which primitive you meant—isolate or clear—and how range XOR is built.
hints.2: Isolate = x&-x; clear = x&(x-1); range = pref[r]⊕pref[l-1]; Hamming = popcount(x^y).
hints.3: List: don't swap isolate/clear; use pref[r]⊕pref[l-1]; Fedor popcount(x^y); AND never increases; encode n≤15–20 used/choice sets as masks.

tradeoffs.topic: Clear lowest set bit (n & (n-1)) vs isolate it (n & -n)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Use n & (n-1) to clear/walk set bits (popcount / Brian Kernighan); use n & -n to isolate the lowest set bit for partitions like Single Number III.

tradeoffs.topic: Enumerate 2^n subsets vs iterate submasks in O(3^n)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Plain subset / choice search uses masks over 0..2^n-1 when n ≤ 20; problems that merge or score every submask of every mask need the (sub-1)&mask loop / O(3^n) submask DP (Grouping).

tradeoffs.topic: Prefix XOR for range XOR vs XOR binary trie for max XOR subarray
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Static range XOR queries use pref[r] ⊕ pref[l-1]; maximizing that quantity over ranges uses a binary trie on 30–31 bits over prefixes.

tradeoffs.topic: Plain 2^n complete search vs bitmask DP (Elevator / Matching)
tradeoffs.strong_answer: On/off enumeration or partition search can be raw 2^n; assignment / elevator / TSP-on-n≤20 needs dp[mask] transitions (add one element or merge a submask) rather than one-shot mask scoring.

gotchas.correction: x & -x isolates the lowest set bit; x & (x-1) clears it—popcount walks use clear; XOR-partition uses isolate.
Use a[l..r] = pref[r] ⊕ pref[l-1] (Range Xor Queries / max-XOR-subarray setups).

gotchas.trap: Checking Hamming distance by comparing bits ad hoc instead of XOR+popcount.
gotchas.correction: Friends iff __builtin_popcount(x^y) <= k (Fedor and New Game).

gotchas.trap: Assuming AND of a subset can beat AND of all elements when AND never increases.
gotchas.correction: AND never increases; Mocha-style optima collapse to the AND of all a_i when that observation applies.

gotchas.trap: Missing the n ≤ 15–20 on/off or used-set cue and not encoding the state as a bitmask.
gotchas.correction: Lock dials / team splits / partitions → 2^n masks; assignment / elevator / TSP-on-n≤20 → dp[mask] over the used set.
